mainTopic: Family ties of a גר, and which relatives the פסוק ״עַל כֵּן יַעֲזׇב אִישׁ״ forbids to a בן נח
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about a גר who was conceived before his mother converted but born after she converted. Relatives on his mother's side still count for him, and relatives on his father's side do not. רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about his mother's sister who shares only a father with his mother. The ברייתא also permits him his brother's wife, his uncle's wife, and even his father's wife. It then deals with a man who married a woman and her daughter. Because this teaching of רבי מאיר forbids sisters and aunts to a בן נח, it seems to clash with his earlier view. רב יהודה answers that one version follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows רבי עקיבא. Their argument is over the פסוק ״עַל כֵּן יַעֲזׇב אִישׁ אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ״. רבי אליעזר reads it as the two aunts. רבי עקיבא reads it as the father's wife and the real mother. The גמרא tests each reading against the rest of the פסוק, then asks what principle they disagree about, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A convert conceived before conversion but born after it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a גר conceived before his mother converted but born after she converted has maternal relatives but not paternal relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert whose conception was not in holiness, but whose birth was in holiness, has relatives on his mother's side, but does not have relatives on his father's side.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states its basic rule. For this kind of גר, family on his mother's side still counts for marriage, and family on his father's side does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His conception happened when both parents were non-Jews, but he was born after his mother became Jewish. By תורה law a גר is like a newborn with no relatives. Even so, חכמים still treat his mother's side as family, so that he won't think he went from greater holiness to lesser. The father's side is not treated as family. The next lines show what this means in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: His conception (when his mother became pregnant with him)
In holiness, meaning while the mother was already Jewish

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general rule about all converts. It speaks about one who was conceived before his mother converted and born after she converted.

phrases.english: whose conception was not in holiness,
but whose birth was in holiness
he has maternal kinship,
but he does not have paternal kinship.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיְתָה הוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, וְלֵידָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that began just before this section, about a גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר conceived before his mother's conversion and born after it keeps his maternal relatives but not his paternal relatives.

steps.title: Examples: his sister and his father's sister
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains its rule with examples. A sister or father's sister from the mother's side must be divorced. One from the father's side may stay married to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he married his sister from his mother, he must divorce her. If she is his sister from his father, he may stay married to her. If he married his father's sister from the mother, he must divorce her. If she is his father's sister from the father, he may stay married to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks "how so?" and then gives concrete cases to show what "maternal relatives count, paternal relatives don't" means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whenever the family link runs through a mother, he must divorce. When it runs only through a father, he may stay married. This applies even to his father's sister: if she shares a mother with his father, the link runs through a mother, so he must divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an explanation with examples)
He may stay married to her
His sister who shares his mother

phrases.english: How so?
If he married his sister from the mother, he must divorce her;
if she is from the father, he may keep her.
His father's sister from the mother, he must divorce her;
from the father, he may keep her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives practical examples of the rule stated in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sister or father's sister related through a mother must be divorced. One related only through a father may stay married to him.

steps.title: His mother's sister and a disagreement
steps.stepSummary: His mother's sister from the mother must be divorced. About his mother's sister from the father, רבי מאיר says he must divorce her and חכמים say he may stay married to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother's sister from the mother, he must divorce. His mother's sister from the father: רבי מאיר says he must divorce her, and the חכמים say he may stay married to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with his mother's sister. One case is agreed on, and one case is a disagreement between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When his mother's sister shares a mother with his mother, everyone agrees he must divorce. When she shares only a father with his mother, the aunt's own tie to his mother runs through a father. חכמים let him stay married for that reason, just like his father's sister from the father in step 2. רבי מאיר still says he must divorce, and the next step gives his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother's sister (his aunt on his mother's side)

phrases.english: His mother's sister from the mother, he must divorce her.
His mother's sister from the father:
phrases.notes: She and his mother share a father but have different mothers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he must divorce her;
and the Rabbis say: he may keep her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחוֹת הָאֵם מִן הָאָב, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יוֹצִיא, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יְקַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of examples and adds a case that רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His mother's sister from the mother must be divorced. For his mother's sister from the father, רבי מאיר says he must divorce her and חכמים say he may stay married to her.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's general principle
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains רבי מאיר's view: any ערוה forbidden because of a mother's-side link must be divorced, and one forbidden because of a father's-side link may stay married to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי מאיר would say: any forbidden relative who is forbidden because of maternal kinship, he must divorce. One forbidden because of paternal kinship, he may stay married to.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the rule behind רבי מאיר's ruling in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, what matters is whether the relative is connected to him through his mother. His mother's sister is connected to him through his mother, so he must divorce her, even if she and his mother share only a father. For חכמים, what decides it is how the woman herself is related to his parent: a half-sister through a mother is forbidden, and a half-sister through a father is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden relative (a woman forbidden to him for marriage)

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees he must divorce his sister from the mother, his father's sister from the mother, and his mother's sister from the mother. The only argument is about his mother's sister who shares just a father with his mother. רבי מאיר requires divorce because the link passes through his mother. חכמים allow him to stay married.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֶרְוָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁאֵר אֵם – יוֹצִיא,
phrases.english: any forbidden relative who is due to maternal kinship, he must divorce her;
due to paternal kinship, he may keep her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי מאיר's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, any relative forbidden through a maternal link must be divorced, and one forbidden through a paternal link may stay married to him.

steps.title: Wives of relatives and other forbidden relatives are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that this גר may marry his brother's wife, his father's brother's wife, and all other עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is permitted to his brother's wife, and to his father's brother's wife, and all other forbidden relatives are permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by listing relatives who are permitted to this גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women are forbidden to a born Jew only because they are married to his relatives, not because of a blood link through his mother. Since paternal and marriage-based ties don't count for him, they are permitted. The extra words "all other forbidden relatives" seem to add something, and the next step says what.

keyTerms.meaning: His father's brother's wife (his uncle's wife)

phrases.english: And he is permitted to his brother's wife,
and to his father's brother's wife,
and all other forbidden relatives are permitted to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the list of relatives who are permitted to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His brother's wife, his father's brother's wife, and all other עריות are permitted to this גר.

steps.title: The extra phrase includes his father's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that "all other forbidden relatives" comes to include אשת אביו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to include his father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short comment explaining what the extra words "all other forbidden relatives" are meant to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this comment we might think only the wives of brothers and uncles are permitted. The גמרא tells us the wider wording also includes his father's wife, meaning a woman married to his father who is not his mother.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (this phrase comes to add a case)
His father's wife (not his own mother)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברייתא's broad phrase has a specific purpose: the permission extends even to his father's wife.

phrases.english: To include his father's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the extra wording at the end of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrase "all other forbidden relatives" includes אשת אביו, who is also permitted to him.

steps.title: A woman and her daughter, and the mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a convert who married a woman and her daughter. He keeps one and sends the other away. If his wife dies, some allow and some forbid her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married a woman and her daughter before converting, he keeps one and divorces the other. From the start, he should not marry the second one. If his wife died, he may stay with his mother-in-law. Some say he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא about the גר finishes its list of cases with a man married to both a mother and her daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after converting, he cannot keep both women, so one must go. If his wife dies, the two opinions differ about his mother-in-law. The point is that this ברייתא, in רבי מאיר's name, treats relatives like a sister or aunt as forbidden. That clashes with what רבי מאיר said earlier, and the clash sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: takes or keeps as a wife
from the start, before the fact

phrases.english: If he married a woman and her daughter,
he keeps one and sends one away.
And from the start, he should not marry [the second one].
If his wife died, he is permitted to his mother-in-law.
And some say: he is forbidden to his mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא's list of cases after it included אשת אביו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman and her daughter cannot both stay married to him; he keeps one. After his wife dies, the opinions differ about his mother-in-law.

steps.title: Two versions of רבי מאיר, following two different teachers
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says there is no contradiction. One teaching of רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר, and the other follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is not difficult. This one is רבי מאיר following רבי אליעזר, and that one is רבי מאיר following רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה settles the clash between the two reports of רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this point, רבי מאיר was quoted as saying a בן נח is only warned about עריות that carry a death penalty. This ברייתא, though, forbids a sister or an aunt, which carry only כרת. רב יהודה explains that each teaching of רבי מאיר follows a different earlier view, one following רבי אליעזר and one following רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not changing his mind here. Each of his teachings follows the reading of a different earlier teacher.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: It is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: this one is Rabbi Meir according to Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא we just learned, which forbids aunts and sisters.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: and that one is Rabbi Meir according to Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: This is the earlier statement, that only death-penalty עריות apply to a בן נח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between this ברייתא and רבי מאיר's earlier statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: each teaching follows a different teacher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seemed to contradict himself about whether a sister or an aunt is forbidden to a בן נח.
steps.terutzMaskana: He reported two different views, one from רבי אליעזר and one from רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The argument over ״עַל כֵּן יַעֲזׇב אִישׁ אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ״
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the source of the disagreement. רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as forbidding aunts. רבי עקיבא reads it as forbidding the father's wife and the mother herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: "Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother." רבי אליעזר says "his father" means his father's sister, and "his mother" means his mother's sister. רבי עקיבא says "his father" means his father's wife, and "his mother" means his actual mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that proves there really are two views, which backs up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachers learn from this פסוק which relatives a בן נח must leave behind. For רבי אליעזר, it includes aunts, even though aunts carry only כרת, so the ברייתא forbidding aunts fits him. For רבי עקיבא, it means only the father's wife and the mother, so a בן נח is not warned about aunts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one פסוק is the source for the עריות forbidden to every בן נח. How widely you read it decides which relatives are included.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל כֵּן יַעֲזׇב אִישׁ אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ״.
phrases.english: "Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother."
Rabbi Eliezer says: "his father" means his father's sister,
phrases.notes: He means a man must leave behind the idea of marrying her, because of his father.

phrases.english: "his mother" means his mother's sister.
Rabbi Akiva says: "his father" means his father's wife,
"his mother" means his actual mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: עַל כֵּן יַעֲזׇב אִישׁ אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that proves רב יהודה's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That there are two views, רבי אליעזר's and רבי עקיבא's, about which relatives a בן נח is warned about.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads בראשית 2:24 in two different ways.

steps.title: The rest of the פסוק: a male, another man's wife, and animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא keeps reading the פסוק. ״וְדָבַק״ excludes a male, ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ excludes another man's wife, and ״בָּשָׂר אֶחָד״ excludes animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And shall cleave" means not to a male. "To his wife" means not to his fellow's wife. "And they shall be one flesh" means those with whom he can become one flesh. This leaves out domestic and wild animals, which do not become one flesh with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes explaining the פסוק, finding more עריות that are forbidden to a בן נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase in the פסוק teaches a limit. Real 'cleaving' is only with a woman. It must be his own wife, not someone else's. And it must be a partner he can become 'one flesh' with, which leaves out animals.

keyTerms.meaning: his fellow's wife, a married woman

steps.whatToRemember: From one פסוק, every בן נח is forbidden in: mother and father's wife (for רבי עקיבא, the father's wife even after the father dies; for רבי אליעזר, both only as married women, and he adds aunts), a male, another man's wife, and animals.

phrases.english: "And shall cleave" means not to a male.
"To his wife" means not to his fellow's wife.
"And they shall be one flesh" means
those who can become one flesh,
phrases.notes: In other words, a partner he can have children with together.

phrases.english: which leaves out domestic and wild animals,
since they do not become one flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the פסוק, a בן נח is forbidden in a male, a married woman, and animals.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר: his father means his father's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again: רבי אליעזר reads ״אָבִיו״ as the father's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי אליעזר says that "his father" means his father's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back one line from the ברייתא so it can study it closely. This sets up a series of questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word in the פסוק says "his father", but רבי אליעזר says it really means the father's sister. The next steps test whether the word could mean something else instead.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא quoted in step 9.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: "his father"
means his father's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 9 to study רבי אליעזר's reading in detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי אליעזר, ״אָבִיו״ in the פסוק refers to the father's sister.

steps.title: Why not the father himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״אָבִיו״ does not mean the actual father. The answer: that case is already covered by ״וְדָבַק״, which rules out relations with a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say it means his actual father? That is already taught by "and he shall cleave", which means not to a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we don't read "his father" plainly as the father himself. It answers that the father is already forbidden by another word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with one's father would be relations with a male. That is already forbidden by ״וְדָבַק״ (step 10). So the word ״אָבִיו״ must be teaching something new, such as the aunt.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say": why not read it this way?
"That is": that case is already covered by another source

phrases.english: Say: his father, literally?
That is "and he shall cleave",
phrases.notes: From step 10: ״וְדָבַק״ teaches that a man may not be with a male.

phrases.english: and not to a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי אליעזר's reading against the plain meaning of the word.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reading of ״אָבִיו״ as the father's sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of the word is the father himself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Already covered by another word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is covered by ״וְדָבַק״ ולא בזכר, so ״אָבִיו״ is free to teach something else.

steps.title: Why not the father's wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״אָבִיו״ does not mean the father's wife. The answer: she is already forbidden as another man's wife through ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say it means his father's wife? That is already taught by "to his wife", which means not to another man's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a second option: maybe "his father" means the father's wife. It answers that she is already forbidden as a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While his father is alive, the father's wife is a married woman. ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ (step 10) already forbids any other man's wife, so a separate word is not needed for her.

keyTerms.meaning: "To his wife": only his own wife

phrases.english: Say: his father's wife?
That is "to his wife"
and not to the wife of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second possible meaning of ״אָבִיו״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "His father" could mean the woman connected to his father, his father's wife.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Already covered by another word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's wife is covered by ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ ולא באשת חבירו.

steps.title: Why not the father's wife after his death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether ״אָבִיו״ could mean the father's wife after the father dies, when she is no longer married. The answer: ״אָבִיו״ must be read like ״אִמּוֹ״, which refers to someone who is a relative by blood, not by marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say it means after the father's death? It must be like "his mother": just as "his mother" is not a relative through marriage, so too "his father" is not a relative through marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. After the father dies, his wife is no longer someone else's wife, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ no longer covers her. The answer is that the two words in the פסוק must match each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, ״אִמּוֹ״ means the mother's sister, who is a blood relative and not a relative through marriage. Since ״אָבִיו״ and ״אִמּוֹ״ sit side by side, ״אָבִיו״ must also mean a blood relative, the father's sister, and not the father's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: After death (here, after the father has died)
Similar to; read in the same way as

phrases.english: Say: after death?
phrases.notes: He means the father's wife after the father dies, when she is no longer married.

phrases.english: It is similar to "his mother":
just as "his mother" is not through marriage,
phrases.notes: For רבי אליעזר, ״אִמּוֹ״ means the mother's sister, a blood relative (step 15).

phrases.english: so too "his father" is not through marriage.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of the father's side. The father's wife is related to him only through marriage. The father's sister is a blood relative. רבי אליעזר's whole point is that ״אָבִיו״ means the blood relative.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the previous suggestion to a case that ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ does not cover.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the father dies, his wife is no longer married, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ cannot forbid her. Perhaps ״אָבִיו״ is needed for that case.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אָבִיו״ must match ״אִמּוֹ״, so both mean blood relatives and not relatives through marriage.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: his mother means his mother's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues with רבי אליעזר's reading: ״אִמּוֹ״ means the mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: "His mother" means his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second word in the פסוק, according to רבי אליעזר. This sets up the next round of questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as ״אָבִיו״ became the father's sister, ״אִמּוֹ״ becomes the mother's sister. The גמרא will now test this reading the same way.

phrases.english: "His mother" means his mother's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ״אָבִיו״ to ״אִמּוֹ״ within רבי אליעזר's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי אליעזר, ״אִמּוֹ״ refers to the mother's sister.

steps.title: Why not the mother herself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״אִמּוֹ״ does not mean the actual mother. The answer: she is his father's wife, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already forbids her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say it means his actual mother? That is already taught by "to his wife", which means not to another man's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why "his mother" does not simply mean his mother. It answers that she is already forbidden because she is married to his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His mother is his father's wife, so she counts as another man's wife. ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already covers her, which leaves ״אִמּוֹ״ free to teach something new.

phrases.english: But say: his mother, literally?
That is "to his wife"
phrases.notes: His mother is married to his father, so she is "another man's wife".

phrases.english: and not to the wife of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the step 12 kind of question, now for ״אִמּוֹ״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of the word is the mother herself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Already covered by another word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother, as the father's wife, is covered by ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״.

steps.title: Why not the mother after the father's death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether ״אִמּוֹ״ could mean the mother after the father dies, when she is no longer married. The answer: ״אִמּוֹ״ must match ״אָבִיו״. Since ״אָבִיו״ is not read literally, ״אִמּוֹ״ is not read literally either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say it means after the father's death? It must be like "his father": just as "his father" is not literal, so too "his mother" is not literal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap: after the father dies, his mother is not married to anyone, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ no longer forbids her. The answer is that the two words must be read the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already showed that ״אָבִיו״ cannot mean the actual father, because ״וְדָבַק״ covers him. Since the two words are a pair, ״אִמּוֹ״ also cannot mean the actual mother, even after the father's death.

phrases.english: But say: after death?
phrases.notes: He means his mother after his father has died, when she is no longer anyone's wife.

phrases.english: It is similar to "his father":
just as "his father" is not literal,
so too "his mother" is not literal.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, ״אָבִיו״ and ״אִמּוֹ״ support each other. ״אָבִיו״ is not about marriage because ״אִמּוֹ״ is not, and ״אִמּוֹ״ is not literal because ״אָבִיו״ is not. So the pair means the two aunts.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 16's suggestion to the case ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ does not cover, just as step 14 did for ״אָבִיו״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the father dies, the mother is not married, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ does not forbid her. Perhaps ״אִמּוֹ״ is needed for that case.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אִמּוֹ״ must match ״אָבִיו״, which is not literal, so ״אִמּוֹ״ is not literal either.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: his father means his father's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא, who reads ״אָבִיו״ as the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: "his father" means his father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies the other opinion in the ברייתא. This sets up questions on רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי אליעזר, רבי עקיבא reads ״אָבִיו״ as a relative through marriage: the father's wife. The גמרא will test this the same way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"His father" means his father's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אליעזר's reading to רבי עקיבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי עקיבא, ״אָבִיו״ refers to the father's wife.

steps.title: For רבי עקיבא: why not the father himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, for רבי עקיבא, ״אָבִיו״ does not mean the actual father. The answer: ״וְדָבַק״ already covers that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say it means his actual father? That is already taught by "and he shall cleave", which means not to a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי עקיבא the same first question it asked רבי אליעזר. It gets the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with the father are relations with a male, which ״וְדָבַק״ already forbids. So ״אָבִיו״ must mean someone else, and רבי עקיבא says it is the father's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall cleave" (to his wife), which rules out a male

phrases.english: But say: his father, literally?
That is "and he shall cleave"
and not to a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the step 12 question to רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of the word is the father himself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Already covered by another word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is covered by ״וְדָבַק״ ולא בזכר.

steps.title: But the father's wife is already covered too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: if ״אָבִיו״ cannot be the father because another word covers him, the father's wife is also already covered, by ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, his father's wife is also already taught by "to his wife", meaning not to another man's wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי עקיבא's own logic against him. If ״אָבִיו״ can't mean what another word already covers, then it can't mean the father's wife either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's wife is married to the father, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already forbids her as another man's wife. That seems to leave nothing for ״אָבִיו״ to add in רבי עקיבא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so": the opening of a challenge

phrases.english: If so,
his father's wife, too,
is "to his wife"
and not to the wife of another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of the step 19 answer to attack רבי עקיבא's main reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading of ״אָבִיו״ as the father's wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the same rule, ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already covers the father's wife, so ״אָבִיו״ would add nothing.

steps.title: It teaches the father's wife after the father's death
steps.stepSummary: The answer: ״אָבִיו״ teaches that the father's wife stays forbidden even after the father dies, when ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ would no longer apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: After death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in two words. ״אָבִיו״ adds the case of the father's wife after the father has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the father is alive, ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ forbids his wife because she is married. Once he dies, she is no longer anyone's wife, so ״אָבִיו״ is needed to keep her forbidden. רבי עקיבא does not need to match the words the way רבי אליעזר did, so this answer works for him.

keyTerms.meaning: After the father's death, when his wife is no longer married

phrases.english: After death.
phrases.notes: Once the father dies, ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ no longer covers her, so ״אָבִיו״ is what keeps her forbidden.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, ״אָבִיו״ forbids the father's wife forever, even after the father's death. ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ alone would only forbid her while the father is alive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי עקיבא can count the father's wife as a separate ערוה for a בן נח, apart from the general ban on a married woman.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a case not covered by the other word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אָבִיו״ seemed to add nothing, since ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already forbids the father's wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אָבִיו״ adds the father's wife after the father's death, when ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ no longer applies.

steps.title: For רבי עקיבא, ״אִמּוֹ״ means his real mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads the word ״אִמּוֹ״ literally, as the man's actual mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״His mother״ means his actual mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out רבי עקיבא's reading of the פסוק. Unlike ״אָבִיו״, which he reads as the father's wife, he reads ״אִמּוֹ״ as the man's real mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, רבי עקיבא read ״אָבִיו״ as the father's wife, not the literal father. Here he says ״אִמּוֹ״ is literal. So for him, a בן נח is forbidden to his own mother.

phrases.english: "His mother" means his mother, literally.
phrases.notes: This is still רבי עקיבא talking. The words come from בראשית 2:24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי עקיבא's reading. After explaining ״אָבִיו״ in steps 18 to 21, the גמרא now gives his reading of ״אִמּוֹ״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי עקיבא, ״אִמּוֹ״ teaches that a בן נח is forbidden to his actual mother.

steps.title: His mother is already covered by ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that his mother is already forbidden, because ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ means his own wife and not another man's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is already taught by ״to his wife״, meaning not the wife of another man!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא. Why do we need ״אִמּוֹ״ to forbid his mother, if ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already forbids her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ teaches that a man may cling to his own wife and not to someone else's wife. A man's mother is his father's wife, so she is already forbidden as another man's wife. That would make the word ״אִמּוֹ״ extra.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as; that is already covered by
The wife of another man (literally, his friend's wife)

phrases.english: That is the same as "to his wife"
phrases.notes: This uses the same kind of challenge as step 20, now aimed at ״אִמּוֹ״ instead of ״אָבִיו״.

phrases.english: and not to the wife of another man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 22 by claiming it repeats what ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading of ״אִמּוֹ״ as the actual mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man's mother is his father's wife. ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ already forbids the wife of another man, so ״אִמּוֹ״ seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: A mother the father forced and never married
steps.stepSummary: ״אִמּוֹ״ is needed for a mother whom the father forced and never married, since she was never his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to his mother whom his father forced, so she was never his father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. ״אִמּוֹ″ teaches about a case that ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ cannot cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father forced the woman and never married her, she is not ״another man's wife″. Then ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ would not forbid her to the son. So ״אִמּוֹ״ is needed to teach that she is still forbidden to him, because she is his mother.

keyTerms.meaning: From the woman he (the father) forced, whom he never married
A woman who was forced (not married)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא: ״אָבִיו״ is the father's wife, even after the father dies. ״אִמּוֹ״ is the real mother, even if the father never married her. Each word covers a case that ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ cannot reach.

phrases.english: His mother, whom his father forced [and never married].
phrases.notes: The father never married her, so ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ does not apply to her. That is why ״אִמּוֹ״ is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by narrowing ״אִמּוֹ״ to a case that ״בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״ does not cover.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (setting up a case that the other word cannot reach)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His mother is always his father's wife, so ״אִמּוֹ״ is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the father forced her and never married her, she is not another man's wife. Only ״אִמּוֹ״ forbids her to the son.

steps.title: What is the real point of the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: Both readings of the פסוק have now been explained. The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא only showed how each one reads the words. Now it wants the deeper reason why they read the same פסוק so differently.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root of the argument)

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" are רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, who read ״אָבִיו״ and ״אִמּוֹ״ in different ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both readings are fully defended, the גמרא steps back and asks for the principle behind the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains why רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא read the פסוק differently.

steps.title: The answer begins with רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by presenting what רבי אליעזר holds. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is only setting up its answer here. It opens with ״רבי אליעזר holds״, and the rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words that follow will explain the principle behind רבי אליעזר's reading. After that, the גמרא will show how רבי עקיבא differs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the opening is given here: the answer starts with רבי אליעזר's principle, and the full answer continues afterward.
